source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Steering, p.9-31

procedures.title: Relay rod (Corvette): remove and install
steps: Fit the spring seat, spring and end plug.
Screw the end plug in until the springs are compressed and the plug bottoms, then back it off 3/4 turn, or as far as needed to line up the cotter pin hole; fit the cotter pin to lock it.
Reconnect the tie rod ends to the relay rod as described under Tie Rods.
Lubricate the tie rod ends and the pitman arm-to-relay rod ball joint.
Refit the steering damper bracket and tighten its bolts; refit the damper as under Steering Damper installation.
Set toe-in and align the steering wheel as described earlier in this section.

procedures.title: Idler arm: remove and install
steps: Removal: remove the idler arm-to-frame nut and bolt (the Corvette uses no washer here).
Remove the cotter pin and nut from the idler arm-to-relay rod ball stud.
Free the relay rod from the idler arm by striking it with a hammer while backing it with a heavy hammer.
Remove the idler arm.
Installation: set the idler arm on the frame and fit its mounting bolts and nuts (no washer on Corvette).
Fit the relay rod to the idler arm with the seal on the stud; fit and tighten the nut.
Fit the cotter pin.
Use the torque values in the specifications at the rear of the manual.

procedures.title: Pitman arm: remove and install
steps: Removal: pull the cotter pin from the pitman arm ball stud and remove the nut.
Free the relay rod from the pitman arm by striking the side of the rod or arm where the stud mounts while backing it with a heavy hammer or similar; pull the relay rod down off the stud.
Remove the pitman arm nut from the sector shaft and mark the arm's position on the shaft.
Pull the arm with tool J-6632 (see figure 3 in the manual).
Installation: fit the arm on the sector shaft on the marks made at removal.
Fit the sector shaft nut.
Place the relay rod on the pitman arm and fit the nut, tightening further only enough to line up a castellation with the stud hole, then fit the cotter pin.

procedures.title: Steering arm: remove and install
steps: Use this when collision or other damage requires replacing a steering arm.
Removal: disconnect the tie rod from the steering arm as described in this section.

Remove the hub cap, dust cap, spindle nut cotter pin and spindle nut, then pull the wheel, hub and drum outward as a unit; if it sticks, back off the brake adjustment (Section 5). On disc brake cars remove the caliper and disc instead.
With these off, reach the steering arm bolt heads and remove the retaining nuts to take the arm off.
Installation: set the arm in place and fit the retaining bolts.
Fit the nuts, using only the special locknut the Chevrolet Parts Catalog lists for this joint.
Pack the wheel bearings with high-quality wheel bearing grease and refit the bearings and wheel/hub/drum, or on disc brake cars the disc and caliper.
Fit the keyed washer and spindle nut and adjust the bearings per Front Wheel Bearing Adjustment in Section 3.
Fit the tie rod ball stud into the steering arm with its dust cover in place.
Fit the castellated nut, tighten it securely and fit the cotter pin.
Check turning (cornering) wheel relationship and toe-in per Section 3 and correct as needed.
